author: John Grisham
introFa: کتاب «The Chamber» نوشته John Grisham یکی از منابع ارزشمند و معتبر برای یادگیری زبان انگلیسی در سطح B2 است. این اثر با ساختاری منسجم و غنی، شما را در تسلط بر واژگان و درک مطلب یاری می‌کند.
readingTipsFa: پیش از مطالعه هر بخش از کتاب «The Chamber»، نگاهی سریع به تیترها و ساختار آن بیندازید.
واژگان و اصطلاحات جدید را در زمینه و بافت جمله یادداشت کنید تا در حافظه بلندمدت تثبیت شوند.
پس از پایان هر فصل، نکات کلیدی و آموخته‌های خود را مرور کرده و به زبان خود خلاصه کنید.

content: with an abridged da capo, and the Ab Impromptu, where everything is beautifully articulate. My review copy had very good piano tone on side 1; rather raw and occasionally distorted on side 2. FRANK DAWES HAYDN Mass no.12 in B flat. Soloists/Westminster Choir/New York PO/Bernstein CBS 76410 (?2.99) If the essence of Haydn's religious wisdom went into The Creation and The Seasons, there was enough left over to colour the 12 surviving masses with the characteristics of their composer's genius. The Harmoniemesse is the last, dating from 1802, a work serene in its assurance, in its masterly deploy- ment of the wind band, and in its occasional re- minders of Die Zauberfiote. Its powerful start belies what is to come: there is sufficient intensity for the moments of drama, but the prevailing impression should be relaxed and otherworldly. Bernstein doesn't quite get this across: the Benedictus, for instance, becomes frivolous, and tempos gallop. Haydn testified to his irrepressible high spirits at the thought of God; Bernstein has been overstimu- lated by the idea. The solo team, capably led by Judith Blegen, produces lovely sounds, the chorus is not always fresh, the orchestra is above praise. The Latin text as printed follows the Arab tradition and omits all mention in the Creed of Christ's crucifixion, passion and death-an endearing aberration. ROBERT ANDERSON JANACEK Idyla for string orchestra. MARTINU Concerto for double string orchestra, piano and timpani. Zden6k Hnat, Oskar Kittner/Prague Chamber Orchestra/Hans-Hubert Schonzeler ,,, RCA LHLI 5086 (?1.99) JANACEK Idyll for string orchestra. DVOIAK Serenade for string orchestra op.22. Southwest German Chamber Orchestra, Pforzheim/Paul Angerer TURNABOUT TV 34532S (?1.29) The coupling of Janacek's Idyll for string orchestra and Dvorak's Serenade for strings makes good sense, for it was Jan6aek's performance of the Dvoirk work in Brno (April 1877) that probably stimulated the composition of his own two works for string orchestra, the Suite (1877) and the Idyll (1888). Though seldom performed and up till now unrecorded, the seven-movement Idyll is a better work than the more familiar Suite. It is more disciplined in its form, more enterprising in its string writing and stylistically hangs together better. After many years of neglect it has now attracted two recordings. One might have expected the RCA record, with a Czech orchestra and Czech flouted in its title (incorrectly; Janacek used two 'I's), to be more authentic. In fact the cheaper Turnabout version is much more convincing. Though so different in style from the mature music, early Jan6aek is equally difficult to bring off; its crabbed pacing and stumbling harmonic rhythm make for many interpretational problems. Schonzeler takes the Czechs through a perfunctory performance that often seems unsure where it is going. Angerer's team, which sounds smaller and is helped by a rich acoustic and a clearer recording, follows every mark in the score with loving care, and lavishes attention on the inner parts. This pays off hand- somely: the hidden rondo of the finale for instance, its opening buried in the cello part and neglected by Schonzeler, is made beautifully clear; the tension of the inner parts against the bland and not very memorable tunes provides the occasional flicker of BASSOONS BY FOX for excellent intonation resonance and projection Catalogue and price list on request Instruments sent on approval Sanderson & Taylor (Edinburgh) Ltd 23 Bruntsfield Place Edinburgh EH10 4HN Tel: 031-229 2051 141 This content downloaded from 129.96.252.188 on Fri, 22 Jan 2016 08:28:08 UTC All use subject to JSTOR Terms and Conditions
